target.domain: unknown; infer conservatively — the supplied document is a theological/argumentative essay on divine self-disclosure (Exodus 3:14, Johannine 'I am' sayings) with a stated project frame ('Theophysics'); no empirical method is specified
target.comparison_class: paper of similar purpose and evidence burden
target.population_boundary: persons and groups explicitly represented in the supplied document; report omissions

gate_results.rationale: The document's load-bearing claims are explicitly framed as report of what Christianity claims, not as established fact (S124, S126, S134-S135), and it names the evidence burden it has not discharged (S091). The one direct citation (S016-S017, Exodus 3:14) is traceable to a named source. However, the Johannine 'I am' sayings (S072-S078) are quoted without citation, and no historical, textual, or translation evidence is supplied anywhere in the document. Factual claims are therefore mostly supported only as claims-about-a-tradition, with the supporting layer deferred.
gate_results.resolution: Not a hard-gate failure: the document does not assert the disputed facts as established. It remains WARN because the deferred support layer (S091) is absent from the supplied unit and the scripture quotations beyond Exodus 3:14 are uncited.

gate_results.rationale: No load-bearing contradiction is present. The apparent tension between reason and revelation is explicitly addressed and held as convergent rather than contradictory (S054, S062-S063, S129-S132). The document also acknowledges that its own arguments may fail (S100) and that revelation claims may be false (S113).

The document stays within its stated scope: describing what Christianity claims and where not to look for God (S043-S045), while explicitly declining to answer every philosophical question (S040-S042) and explicitly deferring historical and evidential questions to a support layer (S091).

The document identifies what would count against it in general terms — revelation can be misunderstood, claims of revelation can be false, Scripture must be interpreted, history must be investigated, the Church can mishandle what it receives (S112-S116) — and concedes some arguments may fail (S100). But it does not state a specific, testable condition under which its own central claim ('God has disclosed Himself') would be judged false.
gate_results.resolution: A kill condition for the central claim is not supplied in this unit; it may be deferred to the referenced support layer.

gate_results.rationale: A cross-domain bridge is asserted between discovery (what the world requires) and disclosure (whom God says He is) at S064-S066, and the document insists the two methods not be collapsed (S062-S063). But the bridge is stated as a posture, not as an explicit mapping with invariants, bridge law, recovery, prediction, alternatives, and kill condition. The 'Theophysics' frame (S062) is named without a stated method.
gate_results.resolution: Bridge elements are gestured at but not formally specified in this unit.

gate_results.rationale: Front matter supplies title, pair_id, sequence, edition, paired article, derivative status, and a support link, and one scripture citation is given with book, chapter, and verse (S016). But the Johannine quotations (S072-S078) carry no citation, and the 'support layer' referenced at S091 is not included in the supplied unit, so its contents cannot be traced.
gate_results.resolution: Partial: metadata and one citation are traceable; the bulk of quoted scripture and the referenced support layer are not.

gate_results.rationale: The document explicitly preserves reader agency: a skeptic need not accept the Bible's authority to follow the argument (S120), the paper disclaims the coercive inference 'Exodus 3:14 is in the Bible, therefore God exists' (S122), and it states the disclosed portrait can be stated honestly before it is proven publicly (S126). No concealed compulsion or destruction of agency appears in the text.
